sweep_summary: The stress-title sweep for Rama (rama1270) surfaced a single item, Kuo 1980 'The prosodic structure of Rama II's klɔɔn' (Journal of the Siam Society 68(2): 15-33). I fetched sources the open PDF from the Siam Society site and the Glottolog record: it is a literary-prosody study of Thai klon verse by King Rama II of Siam, and Glottolog's [rma] assignment is an explicit computerized mis-match on the word 'Rama' (SALA keyword 'Thai: Lit anal', macro-area Eurasia); the text never mentions stress, Nicaragua or Chibchan. Relevance: other-language-or-variety; priority none; it should not enter the Rama bibliography. No first-hand Rama word-stress statement was read in this sweep, so best_new_statement is found=false and the catalog's deciding source (Grinevald/Craig 1988a ms. via StressTyp2 passage 1682, weight-hedged) stands unchanged; the prior audit's held primaries (CIDCA 1987 Diccionario Elemental Rama p. xiii; Chevrier 2012/2017 confirming 'metrical stress as described by Craig') remain the best available, and the unpublished 'A Grammar of Rama' pp. ELAR deposit remains the most likely open location). (/.txt).

audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: every string in the record is verbatim in held files (StressTyp2 dump; Chevrier 2012 pp. 14-15; Chevrier 2017 p. 19). But the classification ('weight-hedged', heavy = CVV+CVC, edge unclear, domain unstated) rests on a database paraphrase of an unpublished 1988/1990 grammar manuscript that we do not hold, with no page and no examples, and StressTyp's own compilers flagged the data as insufficient. Nothing found contradicts the coding: Chevrier (2011 fieldwork, reported 2012/2017) confirms a metrical, non-tonal stress system 'as described by Craig', and the held 1987 CIDCA dictionary introduction (p. xiii) independently says accent has no fixed position and falls as stress on long vowels or higher pitch on some short vowels, which is consistent with weight-sensitivity realized partly by pitch and with WALS 'not predictable'.
